newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel - Bonn will do everything to meet EMU.
newsitem.headline: Waigel - Bonn will do everything to meet EMU.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Tuesday welcomed the results of the Spring report of Germany's six leading economic institutes and said Bonn would do what was within its power to meet the fiscal targets for European monetary union.

Waigel pointed out in a statement that while the institutes noted that Germany still had to do its homework, they acknowleged that it could make a "point landing" and meet the 3.0 percent limit on the deficit in relation to gross domestic product.
"The government will do everything necessary to achieve this goal," he said. "But possible requirements for actions can only be determined after presentation of the May tax estimates."
Waigel said the institutes projected the government's budget deficit to be 3.2 percent of GDP this year, but that this presumed a tax shortfall of 20 billion marks.
"This assumption appears too high in light of the special factors that have influenced tax revenues in the first quarter," he said.
Commenting on cabinet's approval on Tuesday of a reform to Bundesbank laws ahead of monetary union, he said the changes were an "important signal for the creation of EMU".
He also noted that the institutes' report showed that "the conditions for economic recovery continue to remain favourable".
It was now necessary to create the conditions for a recovery on the labour market by lowering taxes and levies.
